description: Flow diagrams: a sankey takes sankeyNodes and sankeyLinks (source, target, value), places the nodes in columns by their depth and draws each link as a ribbon whose width is the value; a chord takes the same nodes and links and arranges them on a circle, the shape for flows that go both ways; specToSankey builds nodes and links from a split spec. Free, in @svgrid/grid.

faq.question: How are the sankey columns decided?
faq.answer: By depth: a node with no incoming links is in the first column, its targets in the next, and so on. Give a node a colour through sankeyNodes; the links take the colour of their source.

faq.question: When is a chord better than a sankey?
faq.answer: When flows run both ways between the same pair, such as exports in each direction. A sankey wants a direction; a chord puts both ribbons between the same two arcs.

faq.question: Can I build the links from rows?
faq.answer: Yes: rowsToChartSpec with a category and a series field, then specToSankey turns that split spec into nodes and links.
